chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Waddad al-Hannat said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'I kiss my young daughter while I am fasting, and something of her saliva enters my mouth.' He said, and he said to me: 'There is no harm; there is no obligation upon you.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْكَ شَيْءٌ: there is no obligation upon you

ai.seo_question: Does kissing a child break the fast in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the transfer of saliva from a young child to an adult during fasting does not break the *sawm*, establishing a specific exception to the general rule regarding ingestion. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic principle that minor, unintentional transfers of moisture from dependents do not constitute a nullifier of the fast, reflecting the practical ease (*yusr*) intended in Islamic law. It serves as a foundational text for discussions on *zawajir* (penalties) and the precise conditions under which the fast remains valid despite minor physical interactions.
